evidence_items.publisher: Help Net Security (reporting OX Security research)

receipt.public_excerpt: Over-specification (80–90%) – AI tools create narrow solutions that cannot be reused. Each variation requires new code instead of small adjustments, producing fragmented systems that are hard to maintain.

evidence_items.explanation: OX's analysis of 300+ repositories found an anti-pattern producing hard-to-maintain systems in 80–90% of AI-generated code.

evidence_items.publisher: Help Net Security (reporting OX Security research)

receipt.public_excerpt: Avoidance of refactors (80–90%) – Unlike experienced developers who refine and improve code, AI stops at “good enough.” It does not restructure or optimize, leading to growing technical debt.

evidence_items.explanation: OX found that most AI-generated code avoids refactoring, which builds up technical debt.

receipt.public_excerpt: AI-generated code is “highly functional but systematically lacking in architectural judgment”, a new report from Ox Security has found.

evidence_items.explanation: Independent coverage of the same report, framed as a new wave of technical debt.

receipt.public_excerpt: Moreover, we did not observe warning signs of degraded code-level maintainability.

evidence_items.explanation: A controlled experiment found no maintainability penalty. But 95% of participants were professional developers co-writing one feature with AI help, which is a different practice from amateur vibe coding.

unresolved_gaps: Few studies isolate code written by amateurs through vibe coding. Most cover AI-assisted code in general.
